pages.title: Read the Line
pages.text: A heatable item shows one line, such as Heat: 794°C - Workable ~17s. This is actual stored temperature. The timer estimates cooling time until the recipe’s minimum workable temperature, not time until cold. Warm/cold items omit it.

pages.title: Item-Owned State
pages.text: Heat survives inventories, drops, storage, and transfers. Cooling uses world time, including unloaded storage, but does not progress while the world is closed. Expired heat can be cleared to merge equivalent cold stacks without losing forging progress.

pages.title: Threshold and Scale
pages.text: Items define maximum temperatures through synchronized server settings. Forge recipes define minimum_temperature (500°C for copper) and heat_ticks (3600 by default, cooling from maximum to 20°C in 180 seconds). The old 25% threshold no longer determines workability.

pages.title: Units and Settings
pages.text: Client heatTemperatureUnit selects CELSIUS, FAHRENHEIT, or KELVIN for item tooltips, Jade, and JEI. All gameplay temperatures remain Celsius. Server settings control crucible ceilings, heating/cooling rates, Bellows hold/decay/cooldown, hunger cost, and item maxima.

pages.title: Hot Castings
pages.text: Crucible outputs leave at actual furnace temperature, capped by their material maximum. Waiting outputs cool. Extraction, hoppers, breaking the station, and dropping never reheat them.

pages.title: Quenching
pages.text: Dropped hot items in water or the filled part of a water cauldron cool ten times faster by default. Hold use on a filled water cauldron with a hot workpiece; release or look away to stop. This physical cooling does not consume water and does not turn copper into annealed copper.

pages.title: Safe Handling
pages.text: At 200°C or above, collect hot workpieces with Primitive Tongs in your other hand, or tagged worn heat protection. Tongs use sticks and twine; no copper is required. Wait for cooling if unprotected. Hoppers can still transfer hot items. Creative players are exempt.

pages.title: Ambient Cooling
pages.text: Colder biomes speed up air cooling; warm biomes slow it. Items keep their last sampled rate while stored. enableAmbientCooling and requireHeatProtection default to true and can each be disabled in server config. The terminal baseline remains 20°C.
